_readme: VERIFIED CORRECTIONS to the DERIVED platform board - applied by build-platform-board.js section 4.
WRITTEN BACK 2026-08-08/09, AND THAT IS WHAT THIS FILE IS NOW FOR: SHRINKING.
This file previously carried a WRITE-BACK QUEUE of 70 entries - 64 amendments plus 6 findings that
existed on the board and in NEITHER release document. All 70 have been written into
RELEASE-2.6.2-TRACKER.md and RELEASE-2.6.2-DEFECT-REGISTER.md, which are the documents the release
is certified against, and deleted from here. The correction layer is not the record.
The six board-only findings SWEEP-01..SWEEP-06 became register defects R262-D-98..R262-D-103. Each
heading names the sweep id it was logged under, so the board history is traceable in both
directions. They were renumbered because the register owns the defect id namespace, and a second
parallel namespace is the exact 'second board' this project keeps having to dismantle.
WHAT REMAINS, AND WHY IT IS NOT LAZINESS. Three SEVERITY corrections, and nothing else. Their
substance - status, evidence, measurement - is in the tracker. The severity is not, because
RELEASE-2.6.2-TRACKER.md HAS NO SEVERITY COLUMN: the board infers P1 from the literal string 'P0'
appearing anywhere in a row, and P2 otherwise. Expressing these three in the document would mean
writing 'P0' into a row where it is false, or deleting a true sentence that happens to contain it.
Both are gaming the parser rather than recording a fact, so neither was done.
THE DURABLE FIX IS A SEVERITY COLUMN IN THE TRACKER, not three more rows here.
ONE FURTHER LIMIT, FOUND DURING THE WRITE-BACK AND WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ADDING ANYTHING HERE:
build-platform-board.js section 1 parses defect headings with the hard-coded pattern R262-D-<n>.
A register entry logged under any other id shape is invisible to the board no matter how well it
is written. That is why the sweep ids were renumbered rather than written in as-is.
DO NOT ADD A STATUS HERE THAT HAS NOT BEEN MEASURED. The sweep's own rule, unchanged.
DO NOT USE THIS FILE TO AVOID EDITING THE RELEASE RECORD. That is what it has just stopped being.

remove.why: PHANTOM. Not an issue — the markdown table header `| File | Shard | Guards | Status |` at RELEASE-2.6.2-TRACKER.md:614, parsed into an item with id `File`, title `Shard` and status OPEN. The generator now rejects table header rows structurally (a row whose next line is the `|---|` separator) and by id shape (a real id is hyphenated and carries a digit), so this cannot recur. Kept listed here so the deletion is a recorded decision rather than a row that quietly vanished.

amend.evidence: SEVERITY P1 RESTORED 2026-08-09. I downgraded this to P2 earlier the same day and WITHDREW that downgrade within the hour, because a control run falsified it — see register R262-D-119. The downgrade claimed 'no code path emits these price ids', evidenced by a grep scoped to web/. A full-repo sweep found TWO runtime readers OUTSIDE web/: api/app/routers/stripe_webhook.py:67-72 maps STRIPE_PRICE_ID_CROWMARK_{SOLO,TEAM,AGENCY}_{MONTHLY,ANNUAL} to tier names at runtime, and apps/portal/src/app/api/stripe/subscriptions/route.ts:30-41 CREATES A SUBSCRIPTION from an env-resolved price id. Railway production carries all six legacy variable names (18 STRIPE_PRICE_ID_* set, measured 2026-08-09; values redacted to this token, so which id each holds is NOT measured). The risk is also differently shaped than either prior note said: not a customer reaching a £399 self-serve checkout (checkout resolves by lookup key and cannot reach these), but an ADMIN creating a subscription at the legacy price through the portal. This row's own gate now binds against it — a price a production env var points at must not be deactivated — so it is NOT safe to execute until the 18 values are read and any pointing at the six are repointed.

SEVERITY P1 → P2, 2026-08-08. The 8 Dependabot alerts are all the astro package, currently Astro 5.18.2; clearing them needs a 5 → 7 MAJOR upgrade, and no attacker-controlled input reaches the vulnerable path on a static build. Real, and not urgent. RETAINED FOR ONE REASON ONLY: the re-assessment IS written into RELEASE-2.6.2-TRACKER.md (row R262-WEB-01) as prose, but the board reads P1 from the literal "P0" inside that row's own true sentence about this site's known invisible-text P0 pairing. Deleting a true sentence to move a board number would be gaming the parser.

SEVERITY P2 → P1, 2026-08-08. RETAINED FOR ONE REASON ONLY: the status, the evidence and the ~146 billed 404 invocations a day are now written into RELEASE-2.6.2-TRACKER.md (row R262-I-04, DONE, commit 4cfe6b11). The SEVERITY cannot be. RELEASE-2.6.2-TRACKER.md has NO severity column, and the board derives P1 solely from the literal string "P0" appearing somewhere in the row — which would be false here. Writing that string in to move a board number would be gaming the parser, not recording a fact.
